To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the approximation ratios of First-Fit-Increasing and First-Fit-Deceasing for the maximum bin size variant of classical bin-packing are (1 + 1/k), and (1 + 2/k), respectively, and that the competitive ratios of various natural algorithms for the maximum bin number variant of classical bin-packings are 1/k, 1/k + 1, and 1/k + O(1).
for the maximum resource variants of bin packing problems, no on-line algorithms are competitive and for the parameterized variants, the problems are NP-hard and W[1]-hard, even for k=2.

for the off-line variant of maximum resource bin packing, the approximation ratios for First-Fit-Increasings and First-Fit- Decreasing are O(1), for the on-line variant of maximum dual bin packing, the competitive ratios for all natural algorithms is infinity and for the on-line classical variant, the competitive ratio for First-Fit-Decreasings is O(1) while for First-Fit and First-Fit-Increaseings it is O(1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
two types of bin packing problems: (1) maximizing the number of bins and (2) minimizing the number of items, where we consider both off-line and on- line variants.

the following problems:Maximum Resource Bin Packing Problem: Given a list of items with positive sizes and a bin size, find an ordering of the items such that the number of bins is maximized, subject to the constraint that no item in any bin is larger than the bin size.

the following problems: maximum resource classical bin packing, maximum resource classical on-line bin packing, maximum dual bin packing, maximum classical bin packing with bounded item sizes, and maximum classical bin packing on-line with bounded item sizes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
First-Fit-Increase is an approximation algorithm for the maximum resource bin packing, that has a worst case ratio of at most 2, and that is optimal in the parameterized case.
the on-line variant of the maximum resource bin packing problems is hard, but the off-line variant is easy.

for the maximum resource off-line variant of classical bin-packing, First-Fit-Decr. is a 2-approximation and First-Fit-Incr. is a 3-approximation; for the on-line variant of classical maximum bin packing, First-Fit is competitive; for the on line variant of dual maximum bin packing, no competitive algorithm exists; and for the parameterized versions, the parameter is not helpful.
